snp1.4:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling amongst the Magadhans on the Southern Hill near the brahmin village Ekanālā.
snp1.4:1.3: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja had about five hundred ploughs yoked up during the sowing season.
snp1.4:1.4: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up his bowl and robe, approached the place where the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja was working.
snp1.4:1.5: Then at that time the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja’s food distribution was proceeding.
snp1.4:1.6: Then the Fortunate One approached the food distribution, and after approaching he stood on one side.
snp1.4:2.1: The brahmin Kasībhāradvāja saw the Fortunate One standing for alms,
snp1.4:2.2: and after seeing him he said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.4:2.3: “Ascetic, I plough and I sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.
snp1.4:2.4: You also, ascetic, should plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing you can eat.”
snp1.4:3.1: “Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.”
snp1.4:3.2: “But we do not see the reverend Gotama’s yoke or plough or ploughshare or goad or oxen,
snp1.4:3.3: but still the reverend Gotama said this:
snp1.4:3.4: ‘Brahmin, I also plough and sow, and after ploughing and sowing I eat.’”
snp1.4:4.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja recited a verse to the Fortunate One:
snp1.4:5.1: “You claim that you are a ploughman,
snp1.4:5.2: but we do not see your ploughing.
snp1.4:5.3: Please tell us about ploughing when asked
snp1.4:5.4: so that we may know your ploughing.”
snp1.4:6.2: wisdom is my yoke and plough,
snp1.4:6.3: conscience the pole, mind is the strap,
snp1.4:6.4: mindfulness is my ploughshare and goad.
snp1.4:7.4: temperance the setting free (of the yoke).
snp1.4:8.4: to that place where, having gone, one does not grieve.
snp1.4:9.1: Thus this ploughing has been ploughed
snp1.4:9.2: that produces the fruit of the deathless,
snp1.4:9.4: one is set free from all suffering.”
snp1.4:10.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja having arranged milk-rice in a large bronze bowl presented it to the Fortunate One, saying:
snp1.4:10.3: the reverend one is a ploughman,
snp1.4:10.4: for the reverend Gotama ploughs the ploughing which has the deathless as fruit.”
snp1.4:11.1: “I will not eat what is gained through chanting verses,
snp1.4:11.2: that is not the Dhamma, brahmin, of those who see,
snp1.4:11.3: Buddhas reject what is gained through chanting verses,
snp1.4:11.4: while Dhamma lasts, brahmin, this is their way of life.
snp1.4:12.1: Another great sage, who is fully adept,
snp1.4:12.2: pollutant-free, at peace regarding worry (about wrong-doing),
snp1.4:12.3: attend to with food and drink,
snp1.4:12.4: for that is the field for those who look for merit.”
snp1.4:13.1: “Then to whom, reverend Gotama, should I give this milk-rice?”
snp1.4:13.2: “I certainly do not see, brahmin, in the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahma, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, princes and men, anyone who, having eaten this milk-rice, could properly digest it, except a Realised One or a Realised One’s disciple.
snp1.4:13.3: Therefore, brahmin, cast away that milk-rice where there is but little grass, or drop it into water which has no breathing creatures.”
snp1.4:14.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja dropped that milk-rice into water which had no breathing creatures.
snp1.4:14.2: Then that milk-rice being thrown into water did hiss and sizzle and steam and smoke,
snp1.4:14.3: just as a ploughshare heated for a day when thrown into water
snp1.4:14.4: hisses and sizzles and steams and smokes, so that milk-rice being thrown into water did hiss and sizzle and steam and smoke.
snp1.4:15.1: Then the brahmin Kasībhāradvāja, anxious, and horrified, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he fell down placing his head at the Fortunate One’s feet, said this to the Fortunate One:
snp1.4:15.3: Just as, reverend Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost, or bear an oil lamp in the darkness so that one who has eyes can see forms, just so has the Dhamma been made clear by reverend Gotama in more than one way.
snp1.4:15.4: I go to the reverend Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks.
snp1.4:15.5: May I receive the going forth in the presence of reverend Gotama, may I receive the full ordination.”
snp1.4:16.1: The brahmin Kasībhāradvāja received the going forth in the presence of the Fortunate One, recieved full ordination.
snp1.4:16.2: Then not long after ordination, venerable Bhāradvāja, while dwelling solitary, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, after no long time (attained) that good for which young gentlemen rightly go forth from the house to the houseless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life, and dwelt having known, experienced, and attained it himself in this very life.
snp1.4:16.3: Destroyed is (re)birth accomplished is the spiritual life done is what ought to be done there is no more of this mundane state - this he knew.
snp1.4:16.4: And venerable Bhāradvāja became another of the Worthy Ones.
